items.prompt: A spinner has three colours. The probability of red is 0.25 and the probability of blue is 0.4. What is the probability of green? Give a decimal.
hints: Add the red and blue probabilities first.

items.prompt: A bag has red, blue and yellow counters. The probability of red is 0.5 and of blue is 0.3. What is the probability of yellow? Give a decimal.
A coin is tossed 100 times and lands on heads 46 times. What is the estimated probability of heads? Give a decimal.
hints: Divide the number of heads by the number of tosses.

items.prompt: In an experiment a drawing pin lands point up 30 times out of 200 throws. What is the estimated probability of landing point up? Give a decimal.
A spinner is spun 50 times and lands on blue 18 times. What is the estimated probability of blue? Give a decimal.
hints: Divide the blue count by the total.
Multiply top and bottom by 2 to make it out of 100.

items.prompt: You roll one die. Which two events cannot happen at the same time?

options.text: rolling an odd number and rolling a 3
options.why: A 3 is odd, so both can happen.

options.text: rolling a 1 and rolling a 6
rolling an even number and rolling a number greater than 3
options.why: A 4 or 6 fits both.

hints: A single roll gives one number.
Look for events with no number in common.
items.explanation: You cannot roll a 1 and a 6 on one roll.

items.prompt: You pick one card from a normal pack. Which two events can happen at the same time?

options.text: picking a heart and picking a spade
options.why: A card cannot be both.

options.text: picking a heart and picking a king
picking a red card and picking a black card
options.why: A card cannot be both.

hints: The king of hearts is one card.
Look for an example card that fits both.
items.explanation: The king of hearts is both a heart and a king, so both events can happen together.

items.prompt: You roll a die. Which pair of events can happen at the same time?

options.text: rolling a 3 and rolling a 4
options.why: A single roll cannot be both.

options.text: rolling an even number and rolling a number more than 4
rolling a 1 and rolling a 2
options.why: A single roll cannot be both.

hints: Find a number that fits both.
A 6 is even and more than 4.
items.explanation: A 6 is both even and more than 4, so both events can happen on the same roll.

items.prompt: Which pairs of events can NOT happen at the same time?

options.text: rolling a 2 and rolling a 4 on one roll
rolling an even number and rolling a 6
options.why: A 6 is even, so they can happen together.

options.text: rolling an odd number and rolling a 5
options.why: A 5 is odd, so they can happen together.

options.text: a coin landing heads and the same coin landing tails

hints: Look for events with no outcome in common.
items.explanation: One coin toss cannot be heads and tails, and one roll cannot be both 2 and 4.

items.prompt: A weather forecast says the chance of rain is 0.2, the chance of cloud with no rain is 0.5, and the rest is sun. What is the chance of sun?

options.why: This is the chance it does not rain.
This is the chance of no rain.

items.prompt: Why do we do an experiment many times to estimate a probability?

options.text: The first trial is always wrong.
options.why: The first trial is not always wrong.

options.text: More trials usually give a better estimate.
To make the probability bigger.
options.why: More trials do not change the true probability.

hints: One toss tells you very little.
Think about tossing a coin 5 times and 500 times.
Results settle down with more trials.
items.explanation: With more trials the results settle closer to the true probability.

items.prompt: A coin is tossed 10 times and lands on heads 7 times. The next student tosses it 1,000 times and gets 507 heads. Whose result is likely to be closer to the true probability?

options.text: The student who tossed 10 times.
options.why: Fewer trials give a less reliable estimate.

options.text: The student who tossed 1,000 times.
They are equally reliable.
options.why: More trials are more reliable.

hints: The true probability for a fair coin is 0.5.
items.explanation: The larger experiment is usually more reliable. Here 0.507 is much closer to 0.5 than 0.7.

items.prompt: A simulation uses a die to act as a spinner with 6 equal sections. What is the probability of each number? Give a fraction.

options.why: There are 6 numbers, not 3.
A probability cannot be more than 1.

items.explanation: Each number has probability 1/6, since six equal chances add up to 1.

items.prompt: A die is rolled 60 times. The number 6 comes up 12 times. What is the estimated probability of rolling a 6? Give a decimal.
A fair coin is tossed 200 times. About how many heads would you expect?
hints: A fair coin has probability 0.5 of heads.

items.prompt: The probability of picking a red sweet from a jar is 0.3. About how many red sweets would you expect in a sample of 50 picks (replacing each sweet each time)?
hints: Multiply the number of picks by the probability.

items.prompt: The probability of an event is 1.2. What does this tell you?

options.text: It is certain to happen.
options.why: Certain events have probability 1.

options.text: There is a mistake, because a probability cannot be more than 1.
It happens more than once.
options.why: Probability is not a count.

items.explanation: A probability is always between 0 and 1, so 1.2 cannot be a probability.

items.prompt: Two events A and B cannot happen at the same time. P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.4. What is the probability that A or B happens?

options.why: This multiplies the probabilities.
This subtracts the probabilities.

items.explanation: For events that cannot happen together, add the probabilities: 0.3 + 0.4 = 0.7.

items.prompt: The probabilities of all the possible outcomes add up to ___.
hints: A certain event has this probability.
items.explanation: The probabilities of all outcomes add up to 1.

items.prompt: True or false: If the probability of rain is 0.3, the probability of no rain is 0.7.

options.text: True
False

items.explanation: The probabilities of an event and its opposite add to 1. 1 - 0.3 = 0.7.

items.prompt: True or false: Three outcomes with probabilities 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 cover all the possible outcomes.

options.text: True
False

items.explanation: 0.2 + 0.3 + 0.4 = 0.9, not 1. Something with probability 0.1 is missing.
